claim_verdicts.evidence: Definition of the lesson's vocab term, worded as the outline item 1 and the glossary entry; no behaviour asserted.

All three files declare `public sealed record OrderMessage(int OrderId, string CustomerEmail, string CustomerName, DateTimeOffset OccurredAt);` in namespaces DonHang.Domain, DonHang.Notifications, DonHang.Payments. OrderMessageContractTests aliases them as Sent, NotificationsCopy, PaymentsCopy.

EfOutbox.cs:19 `Body = JsonSerializer.Serialize(message, message.GetType(), JsonSerializerOptions.Web)`. Docs: "The following options have different defaults for web apps: PropertyNameCaseInsensitive = true; PropertyNamingPolicy = JsonNamingPolicy.CamelCase; NumberHandling = AllowReadingFromString" and "In .NET 9 and later versions, you can use the JsonSerializerOptions.Web singleton".

"By default, if the JSON payload you're deserializing contains properties that don't exist in the plain old CLR object (POCO) type, they're simply ignored." The web-defaults list (configure-options.md) names only PropertyNameCaseInsensitive, PropertyNamingPolicy and NumberHandling, not UnmappedMemberHandling. No UnmappedMemberHandling anywhere in examples/don-hang (grep).

"Prior to .NET 9, constructor-based deserialization treated all constructor parameters as optional" (example `record Person(string Name, int Age)` from "{}" gives `Name = , Age = 0`); "Starting in .NET 9, you can set the RespectRequiredConstructorParameters flag"; "implemented as an opt-in flag in .NET 9". Not in the web-defaults list; no RespectRequired* in the repo (grep). The repo's own test BothCopies_ReadAnOlderMessageWithoutCustomerName asserts a missing string is null.

Round 2 re-read at stage-4: OrderEventsConsumer.cs Read (lines 128-141, identical to the lesson block) and RefundRequestedConsumer.cs:125-127 both deserialise with JsonSerializerOptions.Web and throw PoisonMessageException when message is null, OrderId < 1 or CustomerEmail is null/empty. Payments' queue is bound to donhang.orders with exactly order.refund-requested (Payments/RabbitMqTopology.cs), matching the new §5 clause.

Code: catch (PoisonMessageException) -> `BasicRejectAsync(delivery.DeliveryTag, requeue: false)` (lines 77-81); queue args `x-queue-type: quorum`, `x-dead-letter-exchange: notifications.dead-letter`; DLQ bound with #. RabbitMQ docs (WebFetch summary): messages are dead-lettered when rejected "by an AMQP 0.9.1 consumer using basic.reject or basic.nack with requeue parameter set to false".

outputs/stage-4/scripts/backend/message-shapes.txt is identical to the lesson's output block (12 lines: dead before 0, two `routed: true`, handled yes, Mailpit yes, dead after 1, renamed payload, `reason: rejected`). Script lines 18-22 publish with routing_key order.placed to exchanges/%2F/donhang.orders. Script not re-run.

RabbitMQ DLX page (WebFetch summary): the x-death and x-first-death-reason headers can contain `rejected`, `expired`, `maxlen` or `delivery_limit`; `rejected` means "the message was rejected". Script line 56 prints headers["x-first-death-reason"], captured output shows `reason: rejected`.

OutboxRelay.ClaimDueAsync selects `WHERE published_at IS NULL ORDER BY created_at` and publishes the stored row body; nothing at startup deletes rows. Queue declared durable, quorum; the only QueuePurgeAsync calls in the repo are in DonHang.Tests. Established by code inspection at the tag; an app deploy does not touch the broker.

notifications.order-events.dead is declared with no arguments (no x-message-ttl, no x-dead-letter-exchange back to the main queue) and no service consumes it (only scripts/tests read it), so nothing in the system redelivers it automatically. RabbitMQ DLX page lists dead-lettering triggers only; it describes no automatic return.

Round 2, by inspection (dotnet test not run): line 20 `Body = JsonSerializer.Serialize(Message, JsonSerializerOptions.Web)`; lines 25/34 deserialise with each copy and Assert.Equal the 4-tuple. A rename on a copy loses the value (or breaks the test's compile); a retype to an incompatible type makes the tuple types differ. Only the api's current shape is ever sent, so a reader newly requiring a property in Read is not exercised, as the claim now says.

Code: `QueueBindAsync(Queue, OrdersExchange, "order.*")`, exchange Topic. RabbitMQ docs (WebFetch summary): "For the purpose of routing, the keys are separated into segments by `.`"; "`*` for exactly one segment and `#` for zero or more"; `regions.na.cities.*` matches `regions.na.cities.toronto` but not `regions.na.cities`. Supports the new §7 advice that a two-word key after order. bypasses the binding.

OrderEventsConsumer.cs:117-126: switch over the six listed keys, `_ => throw new PoisonMessageException($"unknown routing key {routingKey}")`; HandleAsync calls SubjectFor before Read. The repo comment above it reads "One subject per routing key", matching the §7 gloss "turns a routing key into an email subject".

Round 3: row 2 now reads 'rejected as poison, or, when Read accepts them but a later step fails, redelivered up to the queue's delivery limit ... then dead-lettered'; claim text synced. The condition matches the code (Read checks only OrderId and CustomerEmail; non-poison failures are nacked with requeue, x-delivery-limit 5) and claim 19. Misread path by NumberHandling = AllowReadingFromString; row 4 by claim 13. Gloss wording: see minor issue.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Follows from claims 4 and 5 (unknown property skipped, missing property left at default) and claims 10-11 (old messages remain). The type-change reasoning holds in the direction that matters: a new reader with a string property cannot read old messages carrying a JSON number (AllowReadingFromString applies to number types reading strings, configure-options.md line 44).
Conditional recommendation ("the rename only tidies a name and nothing forces it"), framed in the lesson as a choice, not a fact; no checkable behaviour.

Both tests compare a 4-tuple of the copies' properties; a fifth api property is unmapped for each copy and skipped by default (missing-members.md line 12: "they're simply ignored"). The third test does not use Body. Established by inspection; `dotnet test` not run in this session.

issues.text: New in round 3 (changed row 2). The gloss defines the delivery limit as the most deliveries of one message. The limit counts returns to the queue, not deliveries: RabbitMQ dead-letters a message 'redelivered more times than the limit', and the repo's own comment on x-delivery-limit 5 says 'its 6th failed delivery is its last'. Off by one against the code the lesson cites.
